title: A galaxy festooned with stellar nurseries
caption: Barred spiral galaxy NGC 4700, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 4700 · constellation Virgo · about 50 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Bright, pinkish clouds are scattered through NGC 4700 in this Hubble image, signs that the galaxy is busy giving birth to many new stars. It is a barred spiral, similar in structure to the Milky Way, lying about 50 million light-years away in Virgo, the Virgin.

Those pink clouds are H II regions. In them, fierce ultraviolet light from hot young stars makes the nearby hydrogen gas glow. They tend to appear alongside the vast molecular clouds where fresh stars are born, and the young stars ionize the gas around them.

Astronomers study H II regions both in the Milky Way and in other galaxies where they are easy to see. They use them to gauge the chemical makeup of these environments and to learn how that shapes star formation. The first one ever recorded was the Orion Nebula, spotted through a telescope in 1610 by the French astronomer Nicolas-Claude Fabri de Peiresc.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.11 x 2.50 arcminutes) and distance (50 million light years), the frame spans roughly 45,000 × 36,000 light-years. Its light set out about 50 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image was taken with Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys through a red filter and a hydrogen-alpha filter that picks out glowing hydrogen. The color assigned to each filter is not published.
understand.eye: The hydrogen-alpha filter isolates the glow of hydrogen gas, making star-forming clouds stand out far more than they would to the eye.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: William Herschel discovered NGC 4700 in March 1786 and described it as a 'very faint nebula'. Because the Universe is expanding, the galaxy recedes from us at about 1400 km/second.
alt: A galaxy dotted with many bright pinkish clouds of glowing gas.
